boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten verified no-admission ways to spend time with art, history, and campus landmarks in Hyde Park.

cards.title: Browse ancient-world galleries
cards.subtitle: 1155 E. 58th St. • UChicago community admission
cards.notes: Bring a valid UChicago ID and take a guest through the archaeology galleries; individual visitors do not need reservations.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost museum visit for UChicago community members and their guests.
cards.evidence_claim: ISAC states that admission is always free for UChicago students, faculty, staff, and their guests with UChicago ID.
cards.source_title: Visit the Museum | Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures
cards.access_notes: Free with a valid UChicago ID for community members and their guests; individual visits require no reservation.

cards.title: Walk the gallery floors
cards.subtitle: 5020 S. Cornell Ave. • Hyde Park
cards.notes: Meet at the front desk, then move through current exhibitions and the D’Angelo Library without buying anything.
cards.short_summary: A public contemporary-art stop with galleries and a public library.
cards.evidence_claim: Hyde Park Art Center says it is free and open to the public, and that its D’Angelo Library is always open to the public.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Hyde Park Art Center
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during posted building hours; check the visit page for holiday or special-event changes.

cards.title: Circle Henry Moore’s Nuclear Energy
cards.subtitle: Ellis Avenue between 56th and 57th Streets • public-art walk
cards.notes: Walk around the twelve-foot bronze memorial and compare its exterior form with the open, cathedral-like interior space.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor look at UChicago’s memorial to Chicago Pile-1.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago identifies Nuclear Energy as a twelve-foot bronze sculpture on Ellis Avenue between 56th and 57th Streets.
cards.access_notes: Part of UChicago’s public-art collection; view it from the surrounding public outdoor area.

cards.title: Find the concrete Cadillac
cards.subtitle: Campus North Parking Garage, 5525 S. Ellis Ave. • public-art walk
cards.notes: Use the official artwork page to identify the embedded 1957 Cadillac, then discuss what makes an everyday car an artwork.
cards.short_summary: A monumental outdoor Fluxus work built around a 1957 Cadillac.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago locates Wolf Vostell’s Concrete Traffic at the Campus North Parking Garage, 5525 South Ellis Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Part of UChicago’s public-art collection; view from publicly accessible outdoor campus space.

cards.title: Study Forecast’s angled beams
cards.subtitle: Near Court Theatre, 5535 S. Ellis Ave. • public-art walk
cards.notes: Pause near the Court Theatre entrance and trace the painted aluminum beams from their ground supports to their high joints.
cards.short_summary: A campus sculpture built from brightly painted, intersecting aluminum beams.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago locates John Henry’s Forecast near the south entrance to Court Theatre at 5535 South Ellis Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Part of UChicago’s public-art collection; view from the outdoor approach to Court Theatre.

cards.title: Spot the bronze tree and stones
cards.subtitle: Booth School of Business courtyard • public-art walk
cards.notes: Find the tree-like sculpture in the Booth courtyard and look closely at the stones balanced among its bronze branches.
cards.short_summary: A tree-form sculpture with stones, installed at the Booth School courtyard.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago states that Giuseppe Penone’s Idee di Pietra was installed in the courtyard of the Booth School of Business.
cards.source_title: Giuseppe Penone, Idee di Pietra (Ideas of Stone)
cards.access_notes: Part of UChicago’s public-art collection; view from the Booth School courtyard when it is accessible.

cards.title: Compare marble and landscape
cards.subtitle: Vera and A. D. Elden Sculpture Garden, 5550 S. Greenwood Ave.
cards.notes: Walk the Sculpture Garden and inspect the marble’s irregular cut surfaces and pink striations from several distances.
cards.short_summary: A carved-marble work in the Smart Museum’s sculpture garden.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago locates Jene Highstein’s Truncated Pyramid in the Smart Museum’s Vera and A. D. Elden Sculpture Garden.
cards.access_notes: The artwork is in the Smart Museum sculpture garden; verify site access before going because the museum reports a summer installation closure.

cards.title: Read Processional’s figures
cards.subtitle: Social Service Administration Building • public-art walk
cards.notes: Look for the human forms within the welded bronze and copper composition, then compare its color against the building’s brick wall.
cards.short_summary: An abstract figurative sculpture at UChicago’s Social Service Administration Building.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago describes Abbott Pattison’s Processional as installed in the Social Service Administration Building at the University of Chicago.
cards.access_notes: Part of UChicago’s public-art collection; view only from publicly accessible building areas.

cards.title: Follow Helen Mirra’s painted indexes
cards.subtitle: Main Quadrangle buildings • public-art walk
cards.notes: Choose two publicly accessible Quad buildings and look along hallways and stairwells for the work’s hand-painted index entries.
cards.short_summary: A distributed text artwork threaded through publicly accessible campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago says Helen Mirra’s Instance the determination appears in publicly accessible buildings on the main quadrangle.
cards.access_notes: Use only publicly accessible buildings and respect any posted access restrictions or classes in session.

cards.entity_name: Living: How concise that you can cry…
cards.title: Locate Jenny Holzer’s bronze plaque
cards.subtitle: Reynolds Club, 57th Street • public-art walk
cards.notes: Walk the first-floor hallway at Reynolds Club and slow down to read the small cast-bronze text plaque in context.
cards.short_summary: A compact conceptual artwork installed in a campus hallway.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago identifies Jenny Holzer’s Living: How concise that you can cry… as a cast-bronze plaque in the first-floor hallway of Reynolds Club.
cards.source_title: Jenny Holzer, Living: How concise that you can cry…
cards.access_notes: Part of UChicago’s public-art collection; view only during Reynolds Club public building access.

warnings: Smart Museum admission is always free, but its visit page reports a temporary installation closure through September 21, 2026, so it is not included as a current hang.
